denomProfiles/assembleias-de-deus-brazil: Brazil's largest Protestant family, planted by two Swedish missionaries in Belém in 1911.
Evangelical, Trinitarian faith with Scripture as the sole rule of faith and practice.
Baptism in the Holy Spirit with speaking in tongues as initial evidence.
Divine healing and the gifts of the Spirit for today.
Premillennial expectation of the rapture of the church.
Evangelism among the urban poor and on the Amazonian frontier.
Holiness through "usos e costumes" (customs), historically dress and conduct codes.
Large conventions and ministries centred on "mother churches".
Growing participation in Brazilian politics through the evangelical caucus.
Believer's baptism by immersion and the Holy Supper.
Congregational singing from the Harpa Cristã hymnal (1922).
Government by pastor-presidents of ministries within national conventions such as the CGADB (1930) and CONAMAD.
Women are generally not ordained as pastors, though some ministries now do so.
Brazilian evangelical politics
Assemblies of God pastors and members are prominent in the Frente Parlamentar Evangélica.
Portuguese-speaking missions
Brazilian Assemblies have sent missionaries to Portugal, Lusophone Africa and the diaspora.
Neo-Pentecostalism in Brazil
Later "third wave" Brazilian churches grew in the space opened by classical Pentecostal growth.
Gunnar Vingren
Co-founder and first pastor in Belém.
Daniel Berg
Co-founder and itinerant evangelist.
Frida Vingren
Preacher, editor and hymn-writer in the early church.
José Wellington Bezerra da Costa
Long-serving president of the CGADB (1988–2017).
People declaring affiliation with the Assembleia de Deus in the 2010 Brazilian census (IBGE).
denomProfiles/yoido-full-gospel-church/t: Seoul megachurch built on cell groups, prayer mountains and the "threefold blessing".
denomProfiles/yoido-full-gospel-church/c: Classical Pentecostal doctrine of the Assemblies of God, including Spirit baptism with tongues.
Cho's "Fivefold Gospel": salvation, the fullness of the Spirit, divine healing, blessing and the second coming.
The "Threefold Blessing" of 3 John 2: spiritual, physical and material well-being.
Faith visualised and spoken in prayer, which critics regard as a form of prosperity teaching.
denomProfiles/yoido-full-gospel-church/f: Home cell groups led largely by women, the backbone of the congregation.
Intense prayer, including early-morning and all-night prayer meetings.
Mission and church planting worldwide and in satellite churches across Seoul.
Social welfare and media, including the Kookmin Ilbo newspaper.
denomProfiles/yoido-full-gospel-church/p: Multiple Sunday services in a sanctuary seating about 12,000.
Fasting and prayer at Osanri Choi Ja-shil Memorial Fasting Prayer Mountain (opened 1973).
Believer's baptism and the Lord's Supper.
Women ordained as pastors and elders.
denomProfiles/yoido-full-gospel-church/i: Cho's book "Successful Home Cell Groups" (1981) was copied by churches worldwide.
Church Growth International (1976) spread Yoido's methods across Asia.
Its model of growth influenced large Korean Protestant churches of many denominations.
denomProfiles/yoido-full-gospel-church/m: Membership claimed by the church in the mid-2000s and widely reported; registered membership counts differ from weekly attendance.
denomProfiles/redeemed-christian-church-: Nigerian Pentecostal giant aiming to plant a parish within reach of everyone.
Evangelical, Trinitarian faith with the Bible as the inspired Word of God.
Holiness and sanctification as a distinct experience, stressed from Akindayomi's day.
Baptism in the Holy Spirit with speaking in tongues.
Divine healing and miracles.
The rapture and the premillennial return of Christ.
Church planting, with the stated vision of parishes within five minutes' walk in developing countries and five minutes' drive in developed ones.
Monthly Holy Ghost Services and the annual Holy Ghost Congress at Redemption City.
Reaching the professional classes through "model parishes" (from 1988).
Education and social projects, including Redeemer's University (2005).
Believer's baptism by immersion and Holy Communion.
All-night prayer, fasting and large convention gatherings.
A centralised hierarchy of parishes, zones, regions and provinces under the General Overseer.
Women ordained as deaconesses and pastors.
African diaspora churches
RCCG parishes, such as Jesus House in London, became central to African communities in Europe and North America.
Nigerian public life
The Holy Ghost Congress draws political leaders, and the church shapes Nigerian Pentecostal culture.
Josiah Olufemi Akindayomi
Founder and first General Overseer (d. 1980).
Enoch Adejare Adeboye
General Overseer since 1981 and former mathematics lecturer.
Foluke Adeboye
His wife, a leading pastor in the church.
denomProfiles/universal-church-of-the-ki: Brazilian neo-Pentecostal church of deliverance, prosperity and a global media empire.
Faith in Jesus Christ as Saviour, with Scripture as authority as taught by the church's bishops.
Spiritual warfare: illness and misfortune are often attributed to evil spirits, which are expelled in deliverance.
Prosperity theology: sacrificial giving as an act of faith that God rewards.
Baptism in the Holy Spirit as empowerment for victory in life.
Deliverance from spirits, frequently identified with deities of Afro-Brazilian religions.
Financial breakthrough and family restoration.
Media: the RecordTV network (bought 1989), radio and the Folha Universal newspaper.
Rapid expansion in Africa, Europe and the Americas.
A weekly cycle of themed services ("chains"), for example for prosperity, health and deliverance.
Campaigns such as the "Holy Bonfire" (Fogueira Santa) of sacrificial offerings.
Believer's baptism by immersion and the Holy Supper.
A centralised hierarchy of bishops and pastors under the founder; pastors are men.
Large temples, notably the Temple of Solomon in São Paulo (2014).
International Grace of God Church
Founded in 1980 by Macedo's brother-in-law and co-founder R. R. Soares.
Worldwide Church of the Power of God
Founded in 1998 by Valdemiro Santiago, a former UCKG bishop.
Brazilian politics
The church is closely linked with the Republicanos party.
Edir Macedo
Founder and bishop, owner of RecordTV.
R. R. Soares
Co-founder who left in 1980.
People declaring affiliation with the Igreja Universal do Reino de Deus in the 2010 Brazilian census (IBGE).
denomProfiles/vineyard/tagline: Evangelical churches practising "power evangelism", healing and intimate worship.
denomProfiles/vineyard/coreDoctrines/0: Evangelical, Trinitarian faith with Scripture as the final authority.
denomProfiles/vineyard/coreDoctrines/1: Kingdom theology: the reign of God is "already and not yet" present, following George Eldon Ladd.
denomProfiles/vineyard/coreDoctrines/2: All believers may minister in the gifts of the Spirit, including healing and prophecy.
denomProfiles/vineyard/coreDoctrines/3: Spirit baptism is not tied to tongues as a necessary initial evidence.
denomProfiles/vineyard/focuses/0: "Doing the stuff": praying for the sick and expecting signs and wonders.
denomProfiles/vineyard/focuses/3: Equipping laypeople for ministry rather than relying on a star preacher.
denomProfiles/vineyard/practices/0: Informal services with extended worship and "ministry time" of prayer.
denomProfiles/vineyard/practices/2: Autonomous local churches within national Vineyard associations.
denomProfiles/vineyard/practices/3: Local churches decide whether women serve as senior pastors (Vineyard USA, 2006).
denomProfiles/vineyard/influenced/0/text: C. Peter Wagner named the "Third Wave" after Wimber's Fuller course "Signs, Wonders and Church Growth" (1982).
denomProfiles/vineyard/influenced/1/text: Wimber's visits to Holy Trinity Brompton and St Andrew's, Chorleywood, shaped British Anglican charismatics.
denomProfiles/vineyard/influenced/2/text: Vineyard songs were among the first of the modern worship genre.
denomProfiles/vineyard/influenced/3/text: The 1994 revival began at a Vineyard church, which was released from the association in 1995.
denomProfiles/vineyard/keyFigures/0/role: Leader of the movement from 1982 until his death in 1997.
denomProfiles/vineyard/keyFigures/1/role: Founder of the first Vineyard Fellowship in 1974.
denomProfiles/vineyard/keyFigures/3/role: Fuller professor who co-taught with Wimber.
denomProfiles/hillsong/tagline: Sydney-born global church best known for its worship music.
denomProfiles/hillsong/coreDoctrines/0: Evangelical, Trinitarian faith with the Bible as the Word of God.
denomProfiles/hillsong/coreDoctrines/1: Baptism in the Holy Spirit and the gifts of the Spirit, from its Pentecostal roots.
denomProfiles/hillsong/coreDoctrines/2: An emphasis on God's blessing and the flourishing of believers, which critics have linked with prosperity teaching.
denomProfiles/hillsong/coreDoctrines/3: The church as a vibrant, culturally engaged community.
denomProfiles/hillsong/focuses/0: Worship music for the global church through Hillsong Worship, United and Young & Free.
denomProfiles/hillsong/focuses/1: Campus churches in major cities around the world.
denomProfiles/hillsong/focuses/3: Conferences, including the annual Hillsong Conference (from 1986).
denomProfiles/hillsong/practices/2: Centralised leadership under a global senior pastor and board.
denomProfiles/hillsong/practices/3: Women in senior leadership, including co-senior pastors.
denomProfiles/hillsong/influenced/0/text: Songs such as "Shout to the Lord" (1994) and "Oceans" (2013) are sung worldwide.
denomProfiles/hillsong/influenced/1/text: Its city-campus model was widely imitated.
denomProfiles/hillsong/keyFigures/0/role: Founder and global senior pastor until 2022.
denomProfiles/hillsong/keyFigures/2/role: Worship leader and writer of "Shout to the Lord".
denomProfiles/bethel-new-apostolic-netwo: Charismatic networks expecting miracles and led by present-day apostles and prophets.
Evangelical, Trinitarian faith, with Scripture affirmed as final authority.
Restoration of the offices of apostle and prophet to govern and guide the church.
"Kingdom now": heaven invading earth through healing, miracles and transformation of society.
Ongoing prophetic revelation, said to be tested by Scripture; critics fear it rivals it.
In some networks, the "Seven Mountain" mandate to influence spheres of culture.
Supernatural ministry and expectation of signs and wonders.
Training through schools such as the Bethel School of Supernatural Ministry (1998).
Worship music, notably Bethel Music and Jesus Culture.
Prophetic ministry and intercession, sometimes with political engagement.
Extended worship with prophetic and healing ministry.
Believer's baptism and communion.
Relational networks under apostolic leaders rather than denominations.
Women serve as pastors and leaders in many networks, including Bethel.
Global worship music
Bethel Music songs are sung in many denominations.
Independent charismatic Christianity
Apostolic networks have spread in Africa, Asia and Latin America.
American politics
Some NAR-linked prophets became prominent in Christian nationalist activism.
C. Peter Wagner
Popularised the term "New Apostolic Reformation" (d. 2016).
Bill Johnson
Senior leader of Bethel Church, Redding, and author of "When Heaven Invades Earth" (2003).
Kris Vallotton
Bethel leader and prophetic teacher.
Che Ahn
Founder of Harvest International Ministry.
denomProfiles/indian-pentecostal-church-: Kerala-born Pentecostal church led by Indians from its founding in 1924.
Evangelical, Trinitarian faith with the Bible as inerrant.
Salvation by grace through faith and new birth.
Baptism in the Holy Spirit with speaking in tongues.
Divine healing, traditionally without reliance on medicine for many members.
The imminent return of Christ.
Indigenous leadership and self-support, free from foreign missionary control.
Evangelism across India and among the Malayali diaspora in the Gulf and North America.
Holiness, expressed in many congregations by not wearing jewellery.
Bible training through Hebron Bible College, Kumbanad (1930).
Believer's baptism by immersion, often of converts from infant-baptising churches.
The Lord's Supper.
The annual Kumbanad Convention.
Government by a General Council with state councils and regions.
Women preach and teach but are not ordained as pastors.
Malayali diaspora churches
IPC congregations are numerous in the Gulf states, North America and Britain.
Indian Pentecostal identity
Its insistence on Indian leadership became a model for other indigenous churches.
K. E. Abraham
Founder and long-serving president (d. 1974).
Robert F. Cook
American missionary who co-worked with the founders.
K. C. Cherian
Early co-worker in the founding of the church.

Headquartered at Kumbanad in Pathanamthitta district, Kerala, the IPC has thousands of congregations across India, strongest in Kerala and also present in Tamil Nadu and northern India; many members are former Syrian Christians or Dalits.
